title: Reconfiguring coaching expertise in datafied sport: From knowledge possession to knowledge orchestration
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Although data and digital analytics are increasingly used in sport, their implications for coaching decision-making and expertise remain insufficiently understood. This study examined how data and digital analytics were incorporated into coaching judgement and decision-making and what these processes meant for the reconfiguration of coaching expertise. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with four coaches, three data and analytics specialists, and three athletes with experience in data-informed coaching in elite and professional sport. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings showed that data did not replace experiential judgement but extended what could be perceived and traced over time, while providing additional grounds on which existing assessments could be reviewed. However, greater access to information did not make coaching decisions self-evident or necessarily more objective. Participants interpreted data's meaning and limitations contextually and selectively weighted diverse forms of evidence. Interpretive work and epistemic authority were distributed among coaches, analysts, and athletes, rendering decision-making more negotiated, whereas authority and accountability for final decisions remained largely with coaches. Taken together, the findings indicated that coaching expertise was being reconfigured around the capacity to orchestrate distributed knowledge, explain, justify, and revise professional judgements, and remain accountable for decisions made under uncertainty. These findings suggest that coach education should extend beyond technical data literacy to develop capacities for contextual interpretation, knowledge orchestration, and accountable professional judgement.

title: Goalkeeper profiles in the English women's super league: Seasonal trends, team-quality contexts, and implications for coaching practice
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Goalkeeper roles in football are increasingly multidimensional, yet goalkeeper-specific evidence in elite women's football remains limited. This study examined goalkeeper match behaviours in the English Women's Super League across seven available seasons, focusing on seasonal trends and team-quality differences. Hudl StatsBomb event data covered 853 matches, 17 teams, and 71 goalkeepers. Goalkeeper actions were grouped into attacking and defensive domains, standardised using per-match and proportional metrics, and analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple factor analysis, Ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and regression models appropriate to count and cluster-membership outcomes. Attacking actions accounted for 80.92% of included goalkeeper actions. Cluster analysis identified two dominant profiles, Possession organiser and Goal defender, alongside two rare, event-defined situational subprofiles, Sweeper and Active intervener. The possession organiser profile was dominant, representing 77.7% of team-match observations, while the goal defender profile represented 15.4%. Across seasons, goalkeeper involvement showed a shift towards greater possession involvement, with increases in passing, carrying, ball receipts, and keeper-sweeper actions. Team quality was associated with differences in goalkeeper profiles: Top 4 teams showed greater possession involvement and more possession organiser profiles, whereas Low-ranking teams showed greater defensive workload and more goal defender profiles. These findings support a layered approach to goalkeeper profiling, in which broad possession- and defence-oriented involvement is interpreted alongside rare but tactically meaningful situational actions.

title: Playing up the ladder: GPS-derived match physical outputs of youth soccer players promoted to a higher age category
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: This study examined the GPS-derived match physical outputs of youth soccer players promoted to compete in a higher age category. A retrospective observational study was conducted using match data collected over three seasons (2022–23 to 2024–25) from an elite youth soccer academy (n = 221). Three questions were examined: (i) whether promoted players differed from their regular teammates when competing in their original age category; (ii) whether they differed from the regular players of the higher age category when competing alongside them; and (iii) whether the same promoted players changed their physical outputs between the two age categories. External load variables included relative total distance, high-speed running, sprint distance, high intensity accelerations and decelerations. In their original age category, promoted players did not consistently differ from their regular teammates, although promoted Under-19 midfielders covered greater high-speed running distance. In the higher age category, promoted players generally showed physical outputs similar to those of the regular players of that category, although promoted Under-19 wingers covered greater sprint distance than regular Under-23 wingers. Within-player comparisons, often based on very few players, revealed position- and category-specific changes, with significant effects for decelerations in Under-16 and Under-19 centre-backs, high-speed running and sprint distance in Under-17 full-backs and strikers, and total distance in Under-19 strikers. These findings suggest that promotion is not associated with a consistent change in match physical outputs, but rather with specific changes according to age category, playing position, and physical variable, supporting individualized approaches to player development.

title: Analysis of attacking and defensive playing styles in the Africa cup of nations under-17 and under-20 soccer tournaments
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Identifying and quantifying the different playing styles used by African youth soccer teams is important for objectively describing tactical approaches and team behaviours. This study aimed to identify and analyse team-match playing-style profiles during the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) Under-17 (U17) and Under-20 (U20) soccer tournaments. The AFCON U17 sample included 68 team-match observations from 34 matches, and the AFCON U20 sample included 60 team-match observations from 30 matches. Data were obtained from the Wyscout platform. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple factor analysis, Ward.D2 hierarchical clustering, and outcome-appropriate regression models with standard errors clustered by team and match. The pooled analysis identified four team-match profiles: (1) limited progression, (2) controlled possession and progression, (3) balanced counterattacking, and (4) direct high-transition duel. Pooled Clusters 2 and 3 had higher estimated goal rates than Clusters 1 and 4 after adjustment for multiple comparisons, and U20 teams had a lower estimated goal rate than U17 teams. No pairwise differences in winning odds between clusters remained significant after adjustment, and no robust association was identified between cluster membership and goals conceded. The findings, therefore, provide stronger evidence for an association with goals scored than with match outcome.

title: Tactical indicators, situational factors, and analytical methods in traditional four-player curling performance analysis: A systematic review and evidence mapping
venue: International Journal of Sports Science & Coaching
abstract: Research on curling has covered technical statistics, tactical strategies, game information, and decision-making modeling; however, definitions of performance metrics, their levels of analysis, and their interpretation across game contexts remain somewhat fragmented. This review systematically integrates original analytical studies on competitive performance and tactical decision-making in traditional four-player curling, identifies technical, tactical, and situational metrics, and outlines their units of analysis, game context, and analytical methods. The study adhered to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and conducted a systematic search of Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus, supplemented by Google Scholar and forward and backward citation searches. The search was finalized on September 17, 2026. Studies meeting the inclusion criteria examined traditional four-player curling or explicitly simulated its competitive performance, game states, scoring structures, or tactical decision-making. A total of 23 reports published between 2001 and 2026 were ultimately included for a narrative synthesis and evidence mapping. The evidence primarily covered game information and statistical analysis; strategies related to the hammer, blank ends, and game states; shot performance and positional roles; and tactical decision-making supported by models or computational methods. The strategic value of the hammer and blank ends depends on the point differential, the number of remaining ends, hammer status, and other game conditions; the significance of shot performance metrics depends on shot task, positional role, competitive level, and tactical context. title: Auditory deprivation impairs badminton players’ stroke and anticipatory performance: a field experimental study
abstract: Background Accurate anticipation and precise motor execution are critical to success in badminton, yet most previous research has focused on visual information, with limited evidence regarding the role of auditory information. The present study used a two-part field design to investigate the effects of auditory information on stroke performance and anticipatory performance in badminton. Methods Thirty skilled badminton players completed both parts of the study in a fixed sequence. Part A employed a within-subjects design to examine the effects of modality type (audiovisual condition vs. visual-only condition) on reaction time and hitting accuracy in a smash-return task under the predictable-shot context (shot depth and direction known in advance). Part B employed the same participants and experimental design, with the addition of eye-tracking technology, to examine the effects of modality type on reaction time, mean fixation duration, and saccade frequency under an anticipatory condition (shot depth and direction unknown). Results In Part A, auditory deprivation significantly reduced stroke scores ( p < 0.001) and increased failure rates ( p < 0.001), but did not affect reaction time ( p = 0.376). In Part B, auditory deprivation prolonged reaction time ( p < 0.001) and shortened mean fixation duration ( p = 0.009), while saccade frequency showed no significant difference ( p = 0.862). Conclusion Auditory deprivation led to declines in both stroke accuracy and anticipatory efficiency in badminton players, indicating that auditory information may play a significant role in athletes’ motor control and perceptual processing. Talent or timing? Skeletal maturity, biological maturation, and the relative age effect in youth athletes: a cross-sectional study from a high-performance sporting environment
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Aim We characterised the skeletal maturity profile, relative age distribution, and sport-type differences in biological maturation within a cohort of selected youth athletes from a high-performance sport environment. Methods Thirty-seven youth athletes (20 male, 17 female; mean chronological age: 14.92 ± 1.81 years) from 21 clubs across 15 sports in Split, Croatia, were assessed during the 2024–2025 competitive season. Skeletal age (SA) was estimated using the validated BAUSport™ SonicBone ultrasound system and compared with chronological age (CA). Athletes were classified as early (SA-CA ≥ + 1.0 year), on-time, or late maturers. Sports were assigned a priori to physical/power-dominant or skill/technical-aesthetic categories. The Relative Age Effect (RAE) was examined via chi-square goodness-of-fit and pairwise odds ratios; the primary sport-type contrast used the Mann–Whitney U test with rank-biserial r as the effect size index. Results Mean SA exceeded CA by 0.77 ± 0.89 years across the cohort, with 29.7% classified as early maturers and only 2.7% as late maturers. A marginal, preliminary RAE was observed ( χ 2 (3) = 8.08, p = 0.044, Cramér's V = 0.27), driven by Q1 overrepresentation (43%) rather than Q4 underrepresentation (24%); only Q1 versus Q3 was nominally significant (OR=4.00, 95% CI [1.34, 11.96]), not surviving Holm correction. The sport-type contrast was large and significant: SA-CA was +1.14 ± 0.81 years in physical/power-dominant sports versus +0.16 ± 0.67 years in skill/technical-aesthetic sports (U = 274.0, p = 0.00043, r = −0.70; Hedges’ g = 1.26, 95% CI [0.55, 1.97]). title: Spatial association network structure and associated factors of inter-provincial public sports service supply efficiency in China
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: This study examines spatial association networks and associated factors of public sports service supply efficiency across 31 provincial-level regions in China. Annual data for 2017–2023 are used for data envelopment analysis (DEA) and overall network measures, while spatial visualization, centrality comparisons, and quadratic assignment procedure (QAP) analyses focus on 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2023. A gravity model combines efficiency, population, and geographical distance, with province-specific row-mean thresholds converting continuous scores into directed binary ties. The results show that: (1) mean relative efficiency is higher in 2023 than in 2017, despite intervening fluctuations, and inter-provincial dispersion declines after 2020. Efficiency scores reflect performance against separate annual reference frontiers. (2) Approximately one-quarter of possible directed ties are present each year, with fluctuations in network density. Centrality comparisons identify multiple prominent nodes across eastern, central, and western China, with Henan particularly prominent. (3) The 2023 block analysis identifies four groups characterized by internal concentrations in the northern and northeastern and eastern coastal and central blocks, outward connections from the latter, and reciprocal connections between the block comprising Guangxi, Hainan, and southwestern regions and the northwestern block. (4) Geographical adjacency has positive QAP regression coefficients, while all six socioeconomic difference matrices have negative coefficients. These patterns are consistent with geographical proximity and socioeconomic similarity within the constructed networks. The findings provide a descriptive basis for investigating regional coordination in public sports service provision.

title: Explainable machine learning audit of attribute rating relationships in Football Manager 2023
abstract: Background Football Manager data contain simulated player attributes generated within a proprietary game environment. They can reveal relationships within the rating system but cannot establish real-world talent-identification validity. Objective To audit how baseline attributes predict an internal Football Manager 2023 (FM2023) rating threshold, compare four untuned models under repeated cross-validation, and examine model-specific attribute-contribution stability across categories and positions. Methods We analyzed 2,282 anonymized male player profiles aged 15–18 years. The outcome was an FM2023 overall score of at least 10. Logistic regression, random forest, radial support vector machine (SVM), and a single-hidden-layer neural network were evaluated with three repeats of stratified five-fold cross-validation. We report receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC; average precision), F1 score, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and Brier score. Logistic-regression contributions were calculated on the logit scale; position-specific top-five stability was evaluated with 1,000 bootstrap samples per modeled position. Results Logistic regression had the highest mean ROC-AUC (0.779 ± 0.033) and PR-AUC (0.380 ± 0.047), whereas the neural network had the highest mean F1 score (0.284 ± 0.055). At the prespecified 0.50 threshold, logistic-regression sensitivity was 0.132 and specificity was 0.983. Technical, physical, and mental attributes appeared among the ten highest-ranked contributions. title: Energy System Contributions During a Pad-Based Simulation of Full Contact Kickboxing in Highly Trained to World Class Athletes
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Elite Athletics, Measurement, Exercise Physiology Keywords: combat sports, PCr-La-O2 method, blood lactate, intermittent exercise, lactate elimination Purpose: This study investigated the energy system contributions during a pad-based full contact kickboxing simulation in highly trained to world class athletes. Methods: Nineteen kickboxing athletes (13 males, 6 females; 4 world class, 6 elite, 9 highly trained) completed a pad-based adaptation of a full contact kickboxing simulation, consisting of three 2-minute rounds separated by 1-minute rest periods. Continuous oxygen uptake was recorded via portable spirometry during the protocol and for 15 minutes afterwards, and blood lactate samples were collected. Energy system contributions were estimated using a three-component model. For the first time, this model incorporated corrections for both anaerobic alactic and anaerobic lactic energy, which were compared against established uncorrected and alactic-corrected-only models. Heart rate and rating of perceived exertion were also recorded to assess physiological and perceptual responses across rounds. A Friedman test compared relative energy system contributions, and linear mixed models tested differences between rounds. Results: Using the fully corrected model, the aerobic energy system contribution was highest (71.5%), followed by anaerobic alactic (22.5%) and anaerobic lactic (6.0%, all pairwise comparisons p < 0.001). This ranking remained unaffected across all calculation variants, but the lactate correction increased estimated net lactate accumulation by ~45%. title: Braid Complexity and Peloton Phase Dynamics
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Sport Science, Statistics, Metascience Keywords: peloton, cycling, braid complexity, phase transitions, collective behavior, Netlogo simulations A peloton is a complex, self-organizing system whose collective behavior is driven largely by energetic coupling, described by the peloton convergence ratio (PCR) and positional ordering, described here as braid complexity (C x *). We formalize peloton phase states by combining PCR with C x *, yielding a coupled energetic-positional index, C x P*. Through time-series segmentation of empirical mass-start data and NetLogo simulations, we develop a phase-space framework comprising compact, stretched, and decoupled states and associated subphases. The inclusion of directional microphases—acceleration (Da) and deceleration (Dd)—reveals a hysteresis-like asymmetry within high-PCR/low-C x * states, indicating a stretched-fatigued (Sf) state as a deceleration-driven counterpart to the standard stretched (S) phase. A multivariate approach provides a useful framework for characterizing self-organized transitions in pelotons and may help inform future study of other self-propelled biological collectives by linking individual physiological limits with group-level structural dynamics.
